items.title: Item 1
items.text: Netflix Heads Up the Week’s Team Rule Breakers Earnings ---------------------------------------------------------- * Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX ) – a Foundational Stock in Stock Advisor, and recommended by both Team Hidden Gems and Team Rule Breakers – brings us a Q2 update Thursday. The stock has fallen in 2026, despite a good start to the year , with management chasing a doubling in annual advertising revenue. * ASML (NASDAQ:ASML ) – beating the S&P 500 by 111% since March 2025’s SA recommendation – is due to post Q2 earnings Wednesday morning, after beating expectations and lifting its full-year sales target in Q1 . items.text:
Selected Q2 Earnings from Team Hidden Gems Recs -------------------------------------------------- * U.S. Bancorp (NYSE:USB ) reveals quarterly progress Thursday, after posting a 4.1% year-over-year (YoY) rise in net interest income in Q1 . Management expects revenue growth between 4% and 6% for the full year. Other banks reporting this week include JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM ), Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC ), Bank of America (NYSE:BAC ), Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS ), and Citigroup (NYSE:C ) – all on Tuesday. * Progressive (NYSE:PGR ) provides its latest update Wednesday, after Q1 showed strong policy growth and higher earnings – with net income and EPS both up close to 10% YoY. * Prologis (NYSE:PLD ), recommended in Hidden Gems and Dividend Investor, reports Thursday, with the year so far dominated by land acquisitions to pursue its big push into the data center business. Feel the pulse for Prologis' first half DividerA message from The Motley Fool

After the dot-com peak, the S&P 500 lost money for a full decade. A broader portfolio of the same 500 stocks gained 65%.

Today, the market is more concentrated than it was at the dot-com peak. The top 10 holdings make up over 35% of the entire S&P 500 — nearly double what it was a decade ago.

History says what happens next tends to favor the stocks everyone else is ignoring.

Tom Gardner built a 50-stock portfolio designed for exactly this shift — spanning innovation, small caps, beaten-up turnarounds, and defensive balance.

And The Motley Fool is investing $100,000 of its own money into it alongside members.

items.title: Item 3
items.text: Markets Uncertain as Inflation Looms --------------------------------------- Markets ended on a high note Friday, after SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHYV ) climbed 13% following its IPO debut – though the Korean stock fell in morning trading today. The S&P 500 gained 1.2% over the week and the Nasdaq rose 1.7%. Futures dipped this morning as the U.S. and Iran continued to trade strikes, with the S&P 500 down 0.5% and the Nasdaq losing 1.4% in early trade. * Price rises set to slow – a little: Major banks lead off the new earnings season, as inflation hits the headlines again. The consumer price index (CPI) print is due Tuesday, expected to show a slowing to 3.8% year over year from May’s 4.2% rise. Analysts expect core CPI dipping slightly, from 2.9% YoY to 2.8%. The producer price index update follows Wednesday, having hit 6.5% in May against the prior-year period. * New Fed chair in the hot seat: Kevin Warsh testifies before Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday, following the latest CPI and PPI releases respectively, as stubbornly high inflation raises the chances of an interest rate hike. Review the Fed's June rate decision Divider --------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 4
items.text: Bought the Dip Hall of Fame: The COVID-19 Crash -------------------------------------------------- The scariest headlines have a funny habit of aging into the best entry points. That doesn't mean today's dip is the dip or that the market can't fall further from here – it absolutely can. But if history keeps whispering one thing to long-term investors, it's this: Fear makes a lousy investment thesis. So, before you do anything you'll regret, let's take a stroll through the Bought the Dip Hall of Fame – starting with what might be its most famous resident. Crack why buying the 2020 crash paid off Divider -------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Today’s Take: The Risk You Never Noticed ------------------------------------------- Karl Thiel I have a feeling I’ll be repeating some of my colleagues here, but it’s worthwhile to just drive the point home: The riskiest thing you can do is not invest. And it’s surprisingly easy! Bull markets look expensive, bear markets look scary, and volatile markets make you want to wait and see what tomorrow will bring. — KARL THIEL • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to share the riskiest thing most investors do without realizing it, or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! See more in Today’s Take Divider ------------
